newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: US to back Danish motion on rights in China.
newsitem.headline: US to back Danish motion on rights in China.

text.p: The United States will support a Danish resolution criticising China's human rights record before the U.N. Human Rights Commission despite Chinese warnings of diplomatic consequences, a U.S. spokesman said on Thursday.

The spokesman for the U.S. human rights delegation in Geneva, told Reuters: "China knows that if it wants to improve bilateral relations with the United States, a good starting point would be for it to make progress on improving human rights in China."
China warned the United States on Thursday that relations could suffer if it continued to support Denmark's resolution to censure Beijing's human rights record at the 53-member forum.

The U.S. spokesman told Reuters: "The U.S. is supporting the draft resolution because we believe that the Human Rights Commission is a fundamentally appropriate forum in which to discuss the human rights situation in China."

Denmark was due later in the day to formally present its text on the China resolution, which the United States is co-sponsoring. On Tuesday, a U.S. human rights official told Reuters that the first draft had at least 12 co-sponsors.

But diplomatic sources said Western support appeared to be crumbling, noting Australia on Thursday announced that it had struck a deal with China to set up a formal bilateral dialogue on human rights and would no longer back the Danish motion.
